why: What a cut's picture is checked for before it is picked (studio2/checks.py): each row is one question a reader answers from the picture, built from the cut as planned. A row is a floor (a failed try cannot be picked) only where calibration bore it out: kept stage-1 pictures pass it, rejected and crossed ones fail it, on every run (calibration below, measured by studio2 checks calibrate). Every other row is advice the deciding agent reads. A new check is a row.

opens_shown.asks: Is the thing shown {opens_means}, as described: {what}?

part_shown.asks: Is {part} clearly visible in the picture?

count_right.asks: How many {part} are there in the picture? (count them)

count_separate.means: a part the plan says is many separate things (a count of 2 or more, a number before its noun in the show rows, or a word of `many`) reads as separate items: the part located on the picture, its crop asked `asks` three ways how many items stand apart, the middle answer over the planned number (capped at 1; `unknown_n` when the plan names no number). Why (2026-10-27, fab c03): the approved first picture showed its 25 wafers as one striped cylinder, the paid video kept it, and no check looked before the sheet.
asks: Count the items in this crop that stand apart from each other - each with a visible gap, slot, background or shadow between it and the next. Lines or grooves on one solid surface are not separate items: a solid block or cylinder with stripes counts 1.

How many separate pieces does this part consist of? Count a piece only where you can see space between it and its neighbours (light or background showing through, or a dark gap). Where the pieces touch and fuse into one mass, that mass is 1, however many lines are drawn on it.

How many individual objects can you tell apart here, each one free of the next (thin discs with air between them each count one; a stack pressed together into one solid block counts 1; nothing of the part counts 0)?
count_separate.many_why: Words for many loose things (a stack, a pile, rows, a bundle, a rack). A grid or an array is many marks on one surface (chips on a wafer): the reader rightly reads it as one piece (calibration 2026-10-27: fab dev c10 and c11's chip grids read 1), so it is not counted here.

flow_room.why_frames: each flow is asked on the picture it runs over (studio2/frames.flow_picture): a flow the change lets loose runs over the picture after it (2026-10-28, canal c05: the water bursts in only once the valve lifts)
flow_room.asks: Is the way {flow} visible and uncluttered, so a line drawn along it would read?

text_free.asks: Is the picture free of any letters, numbers, words, logos or watermarks?

anatomy_ok.asks: Are the people and things in it whole and correctly formed (no extra or missing limbs, nothing melted, merged or impossible)?

same_place.asks: Is it the same place as the reference picture (the last image) - the same kind of room, walls, floor, equipment and look - seen anew?

edit_only_change.asks: Compared with the original (the last image), is this picture the same composition, camera and objects, with only this changed: {change}?

change_shown.asks: Compared with the original (the last image), can you see this change: {change}?

change_read.asks: (a blind viewer, shown the picked first and this last picture with nothing else, says what changed; v1's matcher compares it with the cut's change)
